profile.headline: I build where
profile.bio: I’m Amritjot, a Melbourne-based engineer turning complex problems into useful products. I work across full stack systems, applied AI and data, from civic technology to research in physical reasoning.

projects.title: CoBuild
projects.description: Led the architecture and team delivery of a civic-data platform at GovHack 2025. We brought public datasets, mapping and scoring together to make urban-planning decisions easier to explore, all within 48 hours.
highlights: Connected public datasets, mapping and scoring for urban-planning exploration.
Led technical direction during a 48-hour GovHack build.

projects.title: PIPER
projects.description: My Deakin research compares PPO reinforcement learning with LLM and vision-language approaches on drawing-based physical reasoning. The experiments surfaced stronger trajectory and target performance for PPO, alongside stability limits.
highlights: Compared PPO reinforcement learning with LLM and vision-language approaches.
Observed stronger trajectory and target performance for PPO, with stability limits.

projects.title: DigiSpy
projects.description: An AI and cyber-safety learning platform for children. I’m building structured missions, agent accounts and live teacher controls that turn complex digital concepts into hands-on activities.
highlights: Structured missions and agent accounts for AI and cyber-safety learning.
Live teacher controls support guided classroom activities.

projects.title: BlockAgile & Note Wallet
projects.description: At Antier, I built dashboards and distributed services. BlockAgile reduced manual progress reporting by about 50%; gRPC service work on Note Wallet improved response time by about 30%.
highlights: Built dashboards and distributed services at Antier.
Worked on progress reporting and gRPC response-time improvements.

about.title: Curious enough to research it. Practical enough to ship it.
paragraphs: I completed a Master of Data Science at Deakin after studying computer science engineering. That combination shapes how I work: test assumptions with data, design understandable systems, and build for the people who use them.
I’ve worked with teams across engineering, university and high-volume operations. Each setting has taught me to ask better questions and make systems easier to use.
